pr.title: CS-004: Broaden the named audiences with role-based reading paths
pr.body:
Closes #21. Change set **CS-004** (*Broaden the named audiences with role-based reading paths*).

Builds on #97 (`claude/audience-civil-society-academia`, commit `cdfd6e852`) and completes all 7 `CS-004` requirements and all 8 public comments (`PC-0080`, `PC-0083`, `PC-0141`, `PC-0206`, `PC-0255`, `PC-0507`, `PC-0569`, `PC-0586`).

### Mapping of `CS-004` Requirements and `PC-*` Comments to Revised Blocks

| CS-004 Requirement | Public Comment(s) | Revised Block(s) | Summary of Revision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Simplify the opening statement of 'How to use this guidance'** | `PC-0141` | `how-to-use-this-guidance/p-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-15a51a.md` (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-15a51a`) | Adopts the clearer opening wording requested in `PC-0141`: *"This guidance is organised in a manner that allows individual readers to avoid reading through the entire document. The cards below outline the primary benefits for each user group and provide an approximate page count for that essential pathway. The subsequent matrix delineates, by section, what is fundamental, beneficial or flexible for you. Locate your column and trace it downward through the table."* |
| **2. Provide reading pathways for the main audience groups** | `PC-0080`, `PC-0141` | `how-to-use-this-guidance/t-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1.md` (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`), `how-to-use-this-guidance/t-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757.md` (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757`), `how-to-use-this-guidance/p-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f.md` (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f`) | Adds approximate core-pathway page counts to each audience card in `tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`, differentiates stakeholder-specific reading paths across the section matrix (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757`), and expands the closing guidance note (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f`) on how each audience group (including health-service delivery organisations) navigates component articulations and national-to-facility integration sections. |
| **3. Add a reading path for clinical, professional, patient and civil-society audiences** | `PC-0255`, `PC-0080` | `how-to-use-this-guidance/t-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1.md` (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`), `how-to-use-this-guidance/t-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757.md` (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757`), `how-to-use-this-guidance/p-how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f.md` (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f`) | Adds a 6th audience card and matrix column (**Clinical, Professional, Patient, Community & Civil-Society Audiences**) naming nurses and nursing informaticians, midwives, allied health professionals, community health workers, physicians, pharmacists, public-health professionals, patients, and community representatives, with section-by-section core (`●`), recommended (`◐`), and optional (`○`) markers (~25 pages core pathway). |
| **4. Add or explicitly include civil society, community representatives, academia and health-service delivery organisations, with their roles** | `PC-0206`, `PC-0255`, `PC-0507` | `ch1-introduction/p-1-1-4-a8e0b3.md` (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`), `ch1-introduction/p-1-3-3-ada3f2.md` (`prose:1-3-3-ada3f2`), `ch4-implementing-a-national-digital/p-4-5-1-d0bafb.md` (`prose:4-5-1-d0bafb`) | In §1.1.4 (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`), §1.3.3 (`prose:1-3-3-ada3f2`), and §4.5.1 (`prose:4-5-1-d0bafb`), explicitly includes: (a) **Health-Service Delivery Organisations** (hospital groups, provider networks, primary-care networks, and facility operators) and their responsibility at the national-to-facility boundary to align local systems, actor definitions, data capture points, clinical terminology bindings, and information models with nationally governed specifications; (b) **Clinical Professionals and Professional Bodies** (nurses and nursing informaticians, midwives, allied health professionals, community health workers, physicians, pharmacists, and public-health professionals) as co-governors of domain meaning, clinical safety, and acceptable use; and (c) **Others (Patients, Civil Society, Community Representatives and Academic Institutions)** in inclusive governance, public accountability, translating community needs into national priorities, implementation research, evaluation, and workforce development. |
| **5. Provide a non-technical summary or companion for clinical and patient audiences** | `PC-0569` | `ch2-dpi-h-reference-architecture-fra/p-2-1-4a32c0.md` (`prose:2-1-4a32c0`) | Adds a plain-language introductory paragraph at the start of Section 2.1 (`prose:2-1-4a32c0`) explaining the DPI-F vs DPI-H distinction, the two-layer architecture (foundational shared directories/records vs business services), REDDHI, the full-STAC foundation, interoperability, and conformance in everyday clinical and patient terms. |
| **6. Give REDDHI and STAC prominence in the executive summary with more explanation of the key tables** | `PC-0586` | `executive-summary/p-executive-summary-lead-1ff4b3.md` (`prose:executive-summary-lead-1ff4b3`), `executive-summary/p-executive-summary-lead-c447a8.md` (`prose:executive-summary-lead-c447a8`), `ch2-dpi-h-reference-architecture-fra/p-2-1-2-a219ab.md` (`prose:2-1-2-a219ab`) | Gives **REDDHI** and the **full-STAC** foundation (open **S**tandards, open **T**echnologies, open **A**rchitectures, and open **C**ontent such as WHO SMART Guidelines) explicit prominence in the Executive Summary narrative (`prose:executive-summary-lead-1ff4b3`) and distinct-contributions list (`prose:executive-summary-lead-c447a8`), and expands Section 2.1.2 (`prose:2-1-2-a219ab`) with a plain-language guide to interpreting the Chapter 2 tables and design figures (Table 2.2 on REDDHI capabilities/components, Figure 2.3 on DPI-H design principles, and Table 2.4 on goal-to-capability-to-component mapping). |
| **7. Add simplified diagrams relating registries to business services** | `PC-0083` | `ch3-the-reference-architecture-for-d/p-3-5-3-f22754.md` (`prose:3-5-3-f22754`) | Adds a simplified workflow diagram and step-by-step operational flow in Section 3.5.3 (`prose:3-5-3-f22754`) showing how point-of-service applications, foundational registries (Client, Workforce, Facility, Product), the semantic and longitudinal core (Terminology Service, LIMR, Lifelong Health Record), and business services (CDSE, BPR, Supplier Registry, PHSP, HMIS) interact across routine clinical encounters and population-level reporting. |

### Comment-by-Comment Traceability (`PC-*`)

| Comment | Cited Location / Anchor | How Addressed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PC-0080` | §Audience and Scope (`sec:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead`) | Differentiates stakeholder-specific needs across the reading-path cards (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`), section matrix (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757`), and navigation note (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-68d83f`). |
| `PC-0083` | §Architecture Layers (`sec:3-5-3`) | Adds a simplified workflow diagram and 4-step operational flow in `prose:3-5-3-f22754` relating foundational registries and semantic components to business services. |
| `PC-0141` | §How to use the guidance p.4 (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-15a51a`) | Replaces the opening paragraph in `prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-15a51a` with the suggested revision and adds approximate page counts to the reading-path cards (`tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`). |
| `PC-0206` | §1.1.4 p.12 (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`) | Explicitly includes civil society, community representatives, and academic institutions in §1.1.4 (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`), §1.3.3 (`prose:1-3-3-ada3f2`), and §4.5.1 (`prose:4-5-1-d0bafb`), explaining their roles in inclusive governance, public accountability, implementation research, workforce development, and translating community needs into national priorities. |
| `PC-0255` | §How to use this guidance; §1.1.4; §3.4.5 (`prose:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-ee6add`) | Adds an explicit reading path and stakeholder category for clinical, professional, patient, community, and civil-society audiences in `tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-5f2ce1`, `tbl:how-to-use-this-guidance-lead-7cc757`, `prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`, `prose:1-3-3-ada3f2`, and `prose:4-5-1-d0bafb`, naming nurses and nursing informaticians, midwives, allied health professionals, community health workers, physicians, pharmacists, public-health professionals, patients, and community representatives as co-governors of domain meaning and acceptable use. |
| `PC-0507` | §1.1.4 / §4.5.1 (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`) | Adds **Health-Service Delivery Organisations (Hospital Groups, Provider Networks, Primary-Care Networks and Facility Operators)** in §1.1.4 (`prose:1-1-4-a8e0b3`), §1.3.3 (`prose:1-3-3-ada3f2`), and §4.5.1 (`prose:4-5-1-d0bafb`), describing their use of the architecture at the national-to-facility boundary to align local systems, actor definitions, capture points, terminology, and information models with nationally governed specifications. |
| `PC-0569` | §2 p.24–87 (`prose:2-1-4a32c0`) | Adds a plain-language summary framing at the start of Section 2.1 (`prose:2-1-4a32c0`) for clinical, patient, and public-interest audiences. |
| `PC-0586` | §2 p.26–31 (`prose:2-1-2-a219ab`) | Calls out **REDDHI** and the **full-STAC** foundation explicitly in the Executive Summary (`prose:executive-summary-lead-1ff4b3`, `prose:executive-summary-lead-c447a8`) and expands `prose:2-1-2-a219ab` to explain how clinical and operational readers can interpret Table 2.2, Figure 2.3, and Table 2.4. |

- `bun run check:kg-blocks` (`933 sibling(s) up to date`)
